#3554. Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

If you're switching from Apple Music or Spotify to Tidal, you probably want to bring your playlists with you. Tidal points new users toward third-party transfer tools like TuneMyMusic and Soundizz. They both have a free tier, but they only transfers a few hundred songs gratis. My playlists are way bigger than that. The easy solution is to grumble and sign up for a month, then cancel when your tracks are transferred, but that didn't sit well with me. A playlist is just a collection of song names, so why should I have to pay anything to transfer it? To solve the problem, I came up with a simple script that transfers playlists from Apple Music and Spotify to Tidal. I will not be charging a fee. Here's how it works:

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of new-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection."

On Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. Users can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

If you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

Plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

Tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

Exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:

Mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

My cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

It's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:

Your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

Most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

You have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

This isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.

#3553. 'GTA VI' Breaks Entertainment Records With Historic $3.79 Billion Launch

"Grand Theft Auto VI" isn't just breaking records ... it's stealing the entire entertainment industry's lunch money, raking in a staggering $3.79 billion by the end of its first day going live.

The long-awaited video game finally dropped Thursday after a 13-year wait ... and according to Rockstar Games, it shattered the record for the biggest entertainment launch in history, pulling in nearly $4 billion in worldwide retail sales by the end of its first 24 hours.

To put that jaw-dropping number into perspective ... Taylor Swift's entire "Eras Tour" generated a little over $2 billion in ticket sales across 149 shows spanning nearly two years ... and 'GTA VI' nearly doubled that figure on Day 1.

And the records don't stop there ... Rockstar says the game sold 32.5 million copies before its official release and earned a near-perfect 99 rating on Metacritic, making it one of the biggest gaming sensations ever.

As TMZ previously reported ... some gamers are furious over what they consider the franchise's "woke" makeover, complaining that leading man Jason spends too much time doing chores and playing the devoted boyfriend instead of causing chaos.

But judging by those astronomical sales figures ... Rockstar is laughing all the way to the bank.

#3552. How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’

[Editor’s note: This interview was originally published during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. MUBI will release “Minotaur” in theaters on Friday, November 20.]

World-class Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev (“Leviathan”) returned to the Croisette this year in Cannes competition with “Minotaur,” having recovered from a near-fatal illness. After contracting a severe case of COVID in 2021, he reacted badly to the Sputnik vaccine and was put into a medically induced coma for 14 days. When he came out of it, his arms and legs were paralyzed due to Guillain-Barré Syndrome. He lay flat on his back for a year.

When he left the hospital in Germany in 2022, as he told me while at Cannes this year, he was in a wheelchair. While he says he hasn’t watched TV for 20 years now, “I watched a lot of films online,” he said through an interpreter on the roof of the Palais. “I read some things. I did not know if I would ever be able to walk again, to live again as a normal person. I have still now some consequences. I’m not at my best. I have regained completely the motion of my hands, but I have still a bit of a difficulty walking.” Related Stories How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation A ‘Home Alone’ Legacyquel with Macaulay Culkin in Early Development with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg

But he did manage to shoot his sixth feature film last year, but not in Russia. After nine months of waiting, in the spring of 2023, he let go of one expensive project (“Jupiter”) for which he couldn’t seem to raise funding. “I said, ‘Let’s put it on ice, we’ll come back to it later. I don’t want to sit and wait for years and years for you to find the money. I want to make a film now.'”

So instead the filmmaker focused on a parallel project he had also been developing, an adaptation of Claude Chabrol’s 1969 thriller “The Unfaithful Wife,” starring Stéphane Audran as a well-heeled wife cheating on her husband, which was later remade as “Unfaithful” with Richard Gere and Diane Lane. The result, “Minotaur,” is the “Leviathan” Oscar nominee’s first film in nearly a decade, since 2017’s “Loveless.”

At the same time that the filmmaker was coping with his illness, four years ago, at the start of the Ukraine war, he made the decision to leave Russia and move to Paris. Going home would mean the risk of being considered a traitor or an enemy of the state in Russia. “It might result in us becoming what is called foreign agents; it’s a hard thing,” he said. “Maybe this will happen, maybe not. Let’s not be too pessimistic, but mostly all independent journalists are saying that their oppressions are going to get even harsher, and that I think we have decades ahead of us before things get better.”

His 16-year-old had been studying at a French high school in Moscow before the war. “His French was pretty good,” said Zvyagintsev. “So it was an obvious choice. And also, my wife [has been] in love with France for a long time, she has been learning French for many years. So it was a choice, also for both of them, and for their future.”

How’s his French? “Zero,” he said. “The other reason for me was that France is the homeland to cinema; that’s where cinema was born, and also there are so many cinephiles among spectators. Also here in France, directors have the final cut. In the states, it’s much harder to get in a position where you are not censored; it’s not a producer or someone who decides instead of you.”

The filmmaker set about creating believable Russian locations in Riga, Latvia, which still resembles its neighbor country. “The dormitory suburbs around Riga look exactly like Russian dormitory suburbs,” said Zvyagintsev. “A Russian eye would not be able to distinguish between Russia and Latvia in this instance. As for interiors, Anton’s flat was constructed as a set, so it’s a constructed set, and the villa where the main characters live is a contemporary building, a very modern one, and you could find something exactly like this anywhere.”

When it came to finding his cast, the casting director put out a call for Russian characters of a certain age. “Every actor from anywhere who is interested in working with you, they will send you a video presentation,” said Zvyagintsev. “They can be from Argentina, London, Moscow, Paris, wherever. You send them a scene they have to play, and they make a self-tape for you on their iPhone. Before, I despised self-tapes, but it’s convenient, because now with everybody scattered around the world, it’s the only way for us to work. We could not possibly pay for all the people I wanted to check to come to Riga to make a real-life casting. There were people also from Riga who do speak Russian.”

One serious issue for Russian actors still living in Russia was the possible repercussions of participating in a Zvyagintsev project. “I would talk to them about the script and show them parts of the script, so that they know what they’re getting involved in, because, of course, they were at risk of getting blacklisted,” he said. “Most of them, with heartache, refused to take part in the film, but there was one who accepted, and I’m still completely amazed at his courage. It’s the main part, the main character, [actor] Dmitriy Mazurov. I said to him, ‘Are you sure you want to film with me?’ And he said, ‘If I’m not doing this part, I don’t know what I’m doing in acting.'”

Of course, the filmmaker took a different approach to the Chabrol story. “In the first minute, the story is completely revealed,” he said. “We understand that she is being unfaithful, so then all the film is about observing him, observing her, trying to understand, hesitating, and trying to guess what is going on, and while he observes, the spectator starts doing it along with him. And after the murder, actually, he goes back to this position where he’s mostly observing her reaction to the disappearance of a lover, yeah, and she knows what’s going on, and again it’s about observation.”

The filmmaker loved one bravura sequence that is 20 minutes long without any dialogue at all. “The sequence after the murder, it’s 20 minutes, even a little bit more, with not one subtitle, so you only observe his actions, and there are no words: it’s extremely cinematic in its essence.”

And Zvyagintsev added many telling details from the real world, from corruption to the war. “The Chabrol film is much more classical,” he said. “It follows a pattern: he killed, then he’s discovered, and then he will be punished. And I wanted to break up this classical structure and to invent something different based on our Russian realities.”

Was shooting the movie a physical challenge? “When you are full of inspiration, when you are searching constantly for solutions, the light, the sets, the performance of the actors, you don’t feel fatigued in the same way,” he said. “There is such a joy in making the film that is, in your head, real. I think it’s the best drug there is.”

Next up, he will try and resuscitate “Jupiter.” ” I have met some producers who are interested in it,” he said, “so hopefully we will be able to get it moving again.”

#3551. 25 Best Enemies To Lovers Manhwa Ever

Romance manhwa comes in many forms, but some of the most memorable love stories begin with two people who would rather have nothing to do with each other. Whether their animosity stems from conflicting ambitions, family rivalries, painful misunderstandings, or circumstances that force them into an uncomfortable partnership, these stories thrive on the tension between their protagonists. Watching two characters gradually abandon their resentment and discover an unexpected connection is one of the most satisfying aspects of the enemies-to-lovers genre.

The enemies-to-lovers trope is especially popular in fantasy and otome isekai manhwa, where political intrigue, second chances, arranged marriages, and complicated family histories provide plenty of opportunities for romantic conflict. However, the trope isn't limited to historical settings or villainess reincarnation stories. From dangerous games of manipulation to hilarious workplace rivalries and relationships built on long-standing grudges, there's something for every romance fan. For readers who enjoy watching hostility gradually turn into affection, these manhwa are well worth adding to their reading lists.

Beastly Things has a distinct Twilight vibe, introducing readers to a secret society of werewolves. The story follows Ji-u Han, the pack leader's daughter, who harbors an inferiority complex and resents her father for not choosing her as his successor. The plot kicks off when she meets the actor Yuseung Cheo, who's actually a werewolf hunter seeking to exact revenge on the race that killed his parents. However, Ji-u also intends to use him to secure the power she so deeply craves.

Featuring a series of human murders in addition to the conflict between werewolves and hunters, the webtoon's true appeal lies in its two manipulative protagonists on opposing sides, secretly playing games with one another while inevitably beginning to develop feelings. While it features all the hallmarks of toxic relationships, such as obsession, betrayal, and hidden agendas, Beastly Things proves to be an addictive guilty pleasure that's hard to put down.

The Crown Princess Scandal is a different kind of enemies-to-lovers story, as it sets aside the angst and drama in favor of absurd interactions and protagonists whose only reason for hating each other is their clashing personalities. The webtoon begins with Hwa-Yeong, who reluctantly takes her sister's place in a selection process to become the crown princess.

Webtoon has a little of something for everyone, with well over a million titles to choose from. Here are 20 of the best manhwa on the platform.

Hwa-Yeong just wants to go home, and the crown prince finds satisfaction in not letting her get away with her plans, with the plot delivering all sorts of hilarious bickering between the two. Although it feels more like a simple comedy at first, the humor doesn't overshadow the romance, and even Hwa-Yeong’s antics serve as a catalyst for the characters' emotional growth. The palpable tension between the protagonists and the way their relationship develops make The Crown Princess Scandal an especially cute and lighthearted love story.

The Hand That Once Fed offers a particularly messy interpretation of enemies-to-lovers romance, exploring what happens when a former relationship deteriorates into resentment and a desire for revenge. The story follows Evelyn Winter, a widowed duchess whose seemingly comfortable life is disrupted when Colonel Gilath Black suddenly returns. Once her devoted servant and lover, Gilath now approaches her with accusations of treason and an entirely different attitude toward the woman he once adored.

What makes this relationship particularly compelling is the dramatic reversal of their former positions. Gilath, who was once loyal to Evelyn, has become a dangerous presence in her household, while Evelyn must fight to protect her position and navigate the consequences of their shared history. Neither character is particularly straightforward, and their interactions leave readers questioning whether Gilath wants to rekindle their relationship or destroy the woman who once held his heart. With its exploration of betrayal, obsession, and unresolved feelings, The Hand That Once Fed is an excellent choice for readers who prefer their romances with plenty of psychological tension.

Betrayal of Dignity is a dark historical romance that puts its protagonists in a complicated relationship defined by manipulation, desperation, and conflicting interests. The story follows Chloe Verdier, a young noblewoman struggling to prevent her family from falling into ruin. When her sister Alice disappears with a mysterious man, Chloe finds herself turning to Duke Damien Thisse, a notoriously arrogant and ruthless military hero. His proposal offers a potential solution to her family's problems, but accepting his help means entering a dangerous arrangement with a man she can hardly trust.

Unlike lighter enemies-to-lovers stories, Betrayal of Dignity doesn't shy away from the uncomfortable aspects of its central relationship. Damien's controlling personality and Chloe's determination to protect herself create an ongoing struggle for power, with neither protagonist willing to surrender easily. Chloe is particularly interesting because she isn't simply swept away by the Duke's wealth or appearance; she has her own priorities and must constantly consider the consequences of her decisions. The result is an emotionally complicated romance filled with questionable choices, courtly intrigue, and a relationship that is anything but straightforward.

Frozen Hearts introduces a supernatural variation of the enemies-to-lovers trope, placing its protagonists on opposite sides of a dangerous conflict. The story follows Seolha, a Snow Maiden demon who has concealed her true identity while living among humans. Her carefully maintained disguise becomes increasingly difficult to protect when she attracts the attention of the Northern Prince, a man infamous for hunting and killing demons. Their circumstances eventually lead to Seolha becoming his bride, creating an unusual marriage between two individuals who should naturally be enemies.

The main appeal of Frozen Hearts comes from the secrets and conflicting loyalties surrounding its protagonists. Seolha must conceal her identity while navigating married life with someone whose reputation makes him particularly dangerous to her kind. Meanwhile, the prince must contend with a relationship that challenges the rigid beliefs underlying his demon-hunting activities. Their situation creates plenty of opportunities for suspicion, emotional conflict, and gradual character development. With its winter-inspired fantasy setting and supernatural premise, Frozen Hearts is an especially appealing choice for readers who enjoy watching characters from opposing worlds develop feelings for each other.

Dear Nemesis offers a very entertaining take on the enemies-to-lovers trope, combining reincarnation, aristocratic politics, and a romance built on a complicated history. The story follows Calmia Phlox, who receives a second chance at life after a previous existence that left her determined to reclaim her family's position and secure her future as Countess Phlox. However, her ambitions become complicated when she must compete with her beloved twin brother while navigating the schemes of those around her. Matters become even more interesting when Rudbeckia Matari, her former archenemy, unexpectedly proposes marriage.

Rather than immediately abandoning their differences, Calmia and Rudbeckia approach their engagement as a calculated arrangement, with both having their own ambitions and reasons for accepting the partnership. Their shared history makes it difficult for either to place complete trust in the other, but their political alliance gradually develops into something much more personal. With two intelligent, ambitious protagonists constantly trying to stay one step ahead of each other, Dear Nemesis delivers an especially satisfying slow-burn romance. Its combination of strategic maneuvering, family drama, and gradually developing affection makes it an excellent choice for readers who enjoy seeing former rivals become unexpected romantic partners.

Act Like You Love Me! approaches enemies-to-lovers romance with a considerably lighter touch, combining workplace comedy, celebrity culture, and an unexpected supernatural twist. The story follows Ji-eon, a 25-year-old woman struggling financially while juggling demanding jobs. An unexpected temporary assignment puts her in the position of assisting Doyun Nam, a famous actor whose demanding personality quickly gets on her nerves. After another frustrating encounter, Ji-eon discovers that a seemingly ordinary doll possesses the bizarre ability to control him.

Suddenly, the power dynamic between the two changes completely, giving Ji-eon an opportunity to turn the tables on the celebrity who has made her working life miserable. However, having control over someone and actually understanding them are two very different things. As their interactions become increasingly complicated, the hostility between Ji-eon and Doyun gradually develops into something neither initially expected. The series balances its romantic development with plenty of humorous situations, making it a refreshing alternative to the darker, more emotionally demanding stories associated with the trope. For readers who enjoy workplace romances, bickering protagonists, and unconventional premises, Act Like You Love Me! is an entertaining addition.

As its title suggests, Your Eternal Lies follows a deceitful and morally gray protagonist. In the webtoon, Rosen Walker is a notorious criminal who has successfully escaped from prison twice before falling under the supervision of war hero Ian Connor. Thus, Your Eternal Lies mixes the best of the enemies-to-lovers trope with a sort of cat-and-mouse police hunt aboard a ship that keeps readers in suspense about whether she will manage to escape, as well as the real nature of the charges brought against her.

The story features fantasy elements, such as the existence of witches, yet it also offers a grounded reflection on death and the consequences of war, centering on layered characters, each with their own traumas. Beyond the instant chemistry between the protagonists, Your Eternal Lies plays out like a complex game of chess, with Rosen being a wonderfully cunning and strong female lead, making it quite difficult not to root for her to win.

Adonis, also known as Reminescence Adonis, puts an interesting spin on the enemies-to-lovers trope. Ianna, an expert swordfighter, has already spent one lifetime being Arhad's enemy. Her only goal was to best him in battle, but she failed to accomplish even this. Though Ianna claims she has no regrets, as she teeters on the brink of death, she hopes that she can be reborn as Arhad's knight and ally instead of his enemy in her next life. Fortunately, Ianna's dying wish is heard, and she finds herself in the body of her younger self when she opens her eyes.

The deep, almost obsessive love that eventually develops between Arhad and Ianna also offers plenty of payoff.

Though Adonis does take its sweet time with the romance, the series' engaging characters more than make up for the slow burn. The deep, almost obsessive love that eventually develops between Arhad and Ianna also offers plenty of payoff, making this series an absolute must read, especially for fans of historical romance manhwa.

An especially impressive take on the Snow White fairy tale, Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom is a saccharine and wholesome redemption story for Abigail Freidkin, the iconic evil stepmother. It's essentially a blend of isekai and enemies to lovers, where Baekhap Lee, an overworked children's fashion designer, dies from overwork and reincarnates as Abigail. She quickly embarks on a quest to dote on her daughter, Princess Blanche, while evading icy-cool tensions with her estranged, hostile husband, Sabrian.

Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom is loaded with endearing quirks, such as Abigail's unique villainess quality, where she smiles an inherently malevolent smile even when happy, bewildering her servants and husband. Yet, she muscles through it due to her adoration for her daughter. All the while, Sabrian's hostilities include sabotaging Abigail's gifts for Blanche, believing them to be ill-intentioned, yet maintaining a mere distance from her without outright divorcing or showing intentions to remarry, stoking immediate anticipation for sparks to begin flying between them.

#3547. ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch

Even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a new popcorn blockbuster like “Disclosure Day,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences.

One of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’ How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation

“With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler said. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.”

But while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic.

“When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he said. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.”

#3546. Eight Important Router Settings You Should Check (or Change)

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet. This also makes it a highly valuable target for attackers and can leave your data vulnerable—especially if you simply plug your router in with its default settings unchanged. Whether your router is brand new or it's been a while since you audited your existing setup, these are the key settings to check and change right now.

Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network. WPA3 Personal is the newest standard and the most secure, so if it's available on your router, enable it. It's compatible with devices that support Wi-Fi 6. Some older devices may not work with WPA3, in which case the WPA2/WPA3 Transitional mixed mode is a good alternative. At minimum, set your router to WPA2 Personal (AES).

Some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard. (This is not the same as your network name or wifi password, which you set up later.) Default router passwords are searchable online, which leaves your router's admin settings open to anyone. Once you get into your dashboard for the first time, change the default credentials and enable two-factor authentication for your admin account if available.

While some newer routers do have unique, device-specific defaults, it's a good idea to check this setting and ensure it's secure. If you're prompted to create custom admin credentials during the setup process, do it.

Your network name, or SSID, is how your network appears when you search for available wifi. By default, this may be the name of the router brand or a short string of characters, but you should choose something unique to your network. Make sure there's no identifying personal information, such as your name or house number. While you may be tempted to hide your network and obscure your SSID, this may actually make your information less secure, so keep this setting disabled. You can, however, add "_nomap" to the end of your network name, which prevents your router's physical coordinates from being mapped by location databases.

The password to access your network should also be unique and secure and should not include obvious personal information. One option to keep it memorable and easy to type is to create a passphrase using five to seven unrelated words that, combined, have at least 16 characters.

Being able to log into your router's admin dashboard from anywhere may be useful if you have complex networking needs or troubleshooting issues that often have to be addressed when you're away from home, but it also leaves an entry point open for attackers. Turn off remote management to prevent anyone from accessing your dashboard unless they are on your network. (This is also a great reason to have strong, unique admin credentials.)

Two additional settings that leave your network vulnerable are Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and Universal Plug and Play (UPnP). The former lets users connect to your network with a PIN, which can be vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The latter allows smart devices to easily connect to your network—but this also allows malware to spread more readily. You may need to have UPnP on in order to connect devices initially but should disable it afterward.

Any easy win for your network security is segmenting traffic to different networks, so if one is compromised, the data on the others remain unaffected. Many wifi routers have a "guest mode," which creates a separate SSID and password that you can share with visitors instead of giving them your primary network credentials. You can also set up a separate network for all of your smart home and IoT devices so exploitable vulnerabilities in these devices don't put your computers, phones, and other connected devices at risk too.

Routers run a type of software—called firmware—just like any other device. Firmware controls the router's core functions and is not immune to vulnerabilities, which can be exploited by bad actors. And, just like other types of software, manufacturers occasionally push updates to patch these flaws. Check your router's dashboard to see if automatic updates are toggled on. Some devices require an opt-in for auto updates during setup, so you should enable them if they are off. Some routers may even require manual updates—in this case, set a monthly or quarterly (at minimum) calendar reminder to check for patches.

#3544. The iPhone Duo Is Getting Face Unlock

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Apple is currently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other new features. But for users of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

With the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first new iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software update can introduce new hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

What's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Apple made a big deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That said, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some users may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the new option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

#3543. South Park Season 29’s Record Low Rotten Tomatoes Score Confirms A New Era

Although South Park season 29’s Rotten Tomatoes audience rating might seem surprisingly low at first glance, the show’s most recent response actually makes a lot of sense when considered in the broader context of its history. While The Simpsons has been on the air for longer than South Park and has many more episodes to its name than the Comedy Central hit, no one could deny that South Park is definitely the more controversial of the two shows.

Admittedly, The Simpsons has the controversial character Apu, and a handful of episodes from the ‘90s and 2000s that have aged badly. However, South Park is one of TV’s most controversial shows ever, and the series has remained jaw-dropping in its commitment to boundary-pushing content even after almost three decades on the air. There is probably no other show on TV that could get away with depicting the current US President’s sentient penis flying off his body as he uses the toilet.

However, South Park’s constant controversies can sometimes come at a cost to the series. Fans of the anarchic animated comedy might be surprised to find out that, although most online reviewers of season 29 have been largely positive on an episode-by-episode basis, South Park season 29’s current Rotten Tomatoes audience rating sits at a shockingly low 44%. However, this doesn’t really come as a surprise, and it shouldn’t necessarily worry viewers, given the show’s history.

Longtime South Park viewers will recall that the show has always endured mixed reviews since its 1997 premiere, when plenty of critics called season 1 crass, unpleasant, and un-funny. Since then, some of South Park’s most controversial episodes have undoubtedly caused outrage, but plenty of the show’s more straightforwardly divisive episodes have also simply been written off as purely annoying by fans and critics alike.

Ironically, for a show that’s constantly reinventing itself, South Park viewers and critics historically hate changes to the show’s status quo. The responses to season 4, episode 14, “Pip,” epitomized this issue, as many fans were furious about South Park’s decision to forget about Cartman, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny for a week as the show instead opted to parody Charles Dickens' legendary Bildungsroman Great Expectations. The fact that “Pip” was funny and inventive didn’t factor into frustration with its divergence from South Park’s status quo.

Similarly, season 2’s premiere, “Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus,” was South Park’s most widely hated episode for years since the episode also ignored the show’s main characters. Admittedly, season 1’s cliffhanger ending meant this outing was a straightforward example of South Park’s creators intentionally trolling its fans, but the outsized opprobrium that met the prank highlights the same recurring issue.

Much like South Park making Randy a main character was a divisive fan base-splitting maneuver for years, most of the show’s divergences from its status quo have been with frustration. Even season 17’s serialized three-part ending earned the season a Rotten Tomatoes rating of only 60%, further proving that South Park viewers seemingly don’t take kindly to change.

While an audience rating of 44% might sound fairly brutal, it is worth putting this number in context. South Park season 28’s audience rating is a mere 31%, even though its finale was a hilarious, transgressive Christmas special that managed to tie together a flurry of absurd, utterly disconnected storylines. Meanwhile, the biggest new TV show of 2026, CBS’s SEAL Team replacement Marshals, currently has an audience rating of only 28%.

Within this context, the news that South Park has been hit with mixed reviews hardly seems so out of the ordinary or worrying for the show’s future. That said, it is amusing to see just how much South Park’s audience capture may have worked against the show’s reception. South Park has repeatedly been criticized for typically condemning any major divergence from the social and cultural status quo, so it is perhaps unsurprising that the show has found fans who don’t appreciate change.

For years, most of South Park’s biggest mistakes, from the transphobia of season 23, episode 7, “Board Girls,” to the climate change denial of the original ManBearPig storyline, have been rooted in a defense of the status quo. As such, South Park’s poor critical reception could reasonably be attributed to a pro-status quo show making experimental episodes that intentionally mess with the show’s own status quo.

That being said, South Park season 29’s story also offers another reason for its mixed reception. South Park is a gleefully offensive series, and one that doesn’t pull its punches when aiming at every target under the sun. Inevitably, a vocal portion of South Park’s fan base would eventually become upset with season 29’s brutal skewering of billionaires and Trump, and voice this anger online.

South Park is and always has been, since the original inception of the series, a dark, transgressive political satire, so the show really shouldn’t be earning universally positive audience feedback across the board. The same viewers who might have cheered on episodes like “Board Girls” may well hate to see Trump ruthlessly lampooned in “Billionaire Weenietown,” and vice versa. Like any politically charged series, South Park should ultimately be ruffling the feathers of its viewers at times.

Ironically, it might South Park season 29’s willingness to address controversial topics that makes this outing so divisive. South Park has always claimed to be a series that is willing to take on any event or subject, no matter how taboo, but the show has also been known to lapse into laziness at times when meeting a tight deadline or struggling to find news stories of note to explore.

South America, formerly known as South Park, is already breaking records as audiences have their say on season 29 with a record-breaking rating.

As such, there were always guaranteed to be some fans of South Park who only appreciated the show’s satire when it was aimed at subjects they disliked, and this could account for the show’s divided critical reception in season 29. In any case, the reality is that South Park isn’t going anywhere any time soon, no matter how much its Rotten Tomatoes rating might decline in the meantime.

#3539. Forget 'Stranger Things,' These 10 Sci-Fi Shows Have Better Mysteries

After reading the pilot and the pitch book they prepared, Netflix purchased the entire first season of Stranger Things, which would go on to become one of the streaming giant's most successful pop-cultural sensations so far.

There are plenty of reasons why Stranger Things is a masterpiece, including its many enrapturing mysteries; but there are 10 particular sci-fi shows which are even more effective in their approach to mystery. Full of lingering questions that are only occasionally given cathartic answers, these are some of the greatest sci-fi series that the small screen has ever seen.

The incredible Alex Garland began his career as a novelist, which earned him his first screenwriting gig in Danny Boyle's 28 Days Later. Soon enough, he would make the jump to the director's chair with Ex Machina, and six years ago, he dipped his toes into television with Devs, about a software engineer investigating the secretive quantum computing division of her employer after her boyfriend's disappearance.

One of the best-ever sci-fi shows with eight episodes or less, Devs is a miniseries built entirely on mystery, elevating its premise by tying its core narrative puzzle to high-concept physics and existential philosophy. It's thematically layered and full of fascinating characters, but its many complex mysteries are the main reason why it's such a riveting series from beginning to end.

Originally designed by creator Justin Marks as a feature film script about a cross-dimensional story, Counterpart soon evolved into a TV series starring J. K. Simmons in top form. Its narrative follows Howard, a low-level UN bureaucrat in Berlin who discovers that his agency is guarding a gateway to a parallel dimension, forcing him to team up with his own ruthless spy counterpart.

As far as sci-fi spy shows go, it doesn't get much more riveting or complex than Counterpart, one of the most near-perfect yet forgotten thriller shows of the last decade. Like all the best stories about Cold War espionage — a concept that should sound attractive to any Stranger Things fan — Counterpart blends its cleverly constructed sci-fi elements with an exquisitely slow-burning sense of mystery.

Far more than just one of the most fun shows of the 1990s, The X-Files is one of the most groundbreaking and revolutionary series in the history of network television. A pioneer of online fandom culture, it tells the story of two FBI agents, Mulder and Scully. One is a believer in the paranormal, the other an ardent skeptic, and the two investigate bizarre cases while uncovering a vast government cover-up of extraterrestrial life.

The X-Files is the quintessential blueprint for mystery box science fiction, a form of television that's built entirely on constant mysteries, twists, and surprises. Brilliantly episodic but injected with just the right doses of serialization, it's hugely atmospheric and full of mysteries worthy of endlessly theorizing about — which makes it unsurprising that it continues to have one of the most legendary fandoms in modern television history.

Based on the series of novels of the same name by James S. A. Corey (the pen name of Daniel Abraham and Ty Franck), The Expanse is one of those perfect sci-fi shows worth watching over and over again. It's set in a star system full of Cold War tensions between Earth, Mars, and the asteroid belt, where a group uncovers an alien biotech conspiracy that threatens to tear human civilization apart.

This galactic neo-noir is space opera sci-fi through and through, which makes its target demographic fundamentally different from that of Stranger Things; but those whose favorite part of the iconic Netflix original is the escalating mystery and cosmic horror should absolutely love The Expanse. The whole thing is driven by a plot hook that very much feels like it belongs in a classic hardboiled detective novel, and the vast mystery that comes from that hook is incredible.

Based on Graham Yost's trilogy of novels of the same name, Silo is set in a dystopian future where the last few thousand survivors of humanity live in a sprawling underground bunker, where an engineer uncovers dark secrets about their confinement. What ensues is proof that few streaming giants are doing science fiction quite as well as Apple TV right now.

This is one of those Apple TV sci-fi shows where every episode's a masterpiece, and that's largely thanks to how marvelously the writers were able to translate the many mysteries of Yost's books to the small screen. Much like Stranger Things, Silo relies on the premise that the whole world is a lie and our heroes' attempts to discover the truth only keep putting them in further danger, which makes for a naturally enthralling narrative throughout.

Far ahead of its time, The Prisoner is one of the best forgotten shows of the 1960s, a show so auteur-driven and masterfully surreal that it feels like something that was made just a few years ago. Its story follows an unnamed British intelligence agent who abruptly resigns from his post and is then taken to an inescapable coastal village to be interrogated about the exact reason for his departure.

Often described as one of the most brilliantly bizarre and Kafkaesque shows in the history of British sci-fi television, The Prisoner is a must-see for people who loved it when Stranger Things went all in on the natural oddness of its many sci-fi elements. This is the most foundational template for mystery box sci-fi, a psychologically nuanced masterpiece that truly has no equal.

In Fringe, an FBI agent, an institutionalized mad scientist, and his estranged son team up to investigate unexplainable phenomena that trace back to a dangerous parallel universe. What at first started out as more of an episodic and somewhat generic procedural inspired by The X-Files and The Twilight Zone soon transformed into something far more special and uniquely serialized.

As a result of the many transformations that it saw throughout its run, Fringe is not only one of the most brilliant sci-fi shows of modern times, but also one of the most rewatchable. Under the facade of its "monster-of-the-week" format lies a slow-burning mystery with some of the most richly layered world-building of any multiversal sci-fi show in history, and the whole thing remains consistently entertaining throughout the series' entire run.

Back during the 2000s, it felt like everyone and their grandmother was watching and constantly talking about Lost. It was the series that picked up The X-Files' torch as Hollywood's most prominent mystery box show, telling the story of the survivors of a plane crash as they struggle to survive on a dangerous island while uncovering its many mind-bending mysteries.

Even die-hard fans of the show might agree that it jumped the shark a bit toward its conclusion, but it's still one of the most fascinatingly twist-filled shows in the history of sci-fi. Many shows have tried to replace Lost's spot in the pantheon of mystery box sci-fi, but none have quite managed. Every time you think that you're getting more of a feel for what the show is trying to do, it pulls the rug from under your feet with yet another jaw-dropping reveal.

It's a testament to the talent of creators Baran bo Odar and Jantje Friese that Dark, Netflix's first attempt at a German-language series, ended up being one of the most perfect thriller show masterpieces in history. It's set in a small German town, where four interconnected families embark on a desperate search for answers after a child goes missing, uncovering a multi-generational time-travel conspiracy.

When we're talking about the many great time travel and parallel universe sci-fi shows of the streaming era, it doesn't get much better than Dark. Sure, it's a show so filled to the brim with puzzles and mysteries that it's easy to lose track of everything that's going on, but patient viewers will be treated to some downright cathartic reveals. Well before it reaches its finale, Dark makes a rewatch immediately tempting.

If there's any one show worthy of being considered Lost's successor in the space of pop culture phenomena that have redefined the mystery box sci-fi space, it's Apple TV's Severance, a workplace dramedy unlike any other. It's about a group of office workers at a sinister biotech corporation who have undergone a surgical procedure that divides their memories between their work "selves" and their personal lives.

Just as much as it is a deep thematic study of identity and a scathing critique of unchecked capitalist greed, Severance is also one of the most entertaining—and weirdest—sci-fi shows in recent memory. Every time the writers feel kind enough to feed viewers an answer to one of the show's mysteries, they bring up at least a couple more. The result is a show that, so far, has been absolutely impossible to stop watching.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#3538. The Novilla Bliss is an Amazon best-seller, but is this memory foam mattress worth it? I slept on the budget bed for a month to find out

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Novilla Bliss Memory Foam is an all-foam mattress that’s particularly suited to side sleepers and lightweight back sleepers. I slept on a Full size 10" mattress for a month, along with my husband, and I found it especially comfortable for side sleeping. I was also really impressed with the support it provided, considering its low price. But support at the edges left a lot to be desired and it won't be supportive enough for heavier sleepers, and my hot-sleeping husband found it slept way too warm, too.

Far more supportive than its price would suggest

Not robust enough for stomach sleepers or those over 230lbs

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Insanely popular on Amazon, the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam Mattress is a cheap and cheerful all-foam offering that I freely admit I wasn’t expecting much from. However, there were lots of things about the Novilla Bliss that surprised me in a good way and overall, I was quite impressed by the support considering the mattress’ very reasonable pricing.

Name: Jo PlumridgeAge bracket: 45-55Weight bracket: 100-130lbsPredominant sleep position: Combination sleeper who spends slightly more time on her sideSleep issues: Suffers with back pain which can easily be exacerbated by an unsupportive mattress

It’s not going to rival the very best mattresses on the market but if you’re on a budget, this should definitely be on your radar. With a queen mattress currently priced at $269.99 in the Black Friday mattress deals, I think this is one of the best budget beds currently on the market.

In terms of firmness, I’d suggest that most sleepers will find it at the firmer end of the medium scale. There is sinkage and this is an all-foam mattress, but there’s still some support underneath. I can’t think of any other all-foam mattresses I’ve slept on that are as firm, except for the Nectar Classic Memory Foam. However, I must stress that I’m a lightweight sleeper and my husband, who is lightweight to average weight for a man, found it softer than I did.

Still, we both enjoyed it for side sleeping particularly and, as someone who is ultra fussy about lumbar support, I found it more comfortable for back sleeping than I expected. Motion isolation on the Novilla Bliss is exceptional, and I couldn’t feel my husband moving around at all, but edge support is lacking both when you lie or sit on the edge. I didn’t feel as if I’d actually fall off the bed, but there was some definite tilting.

Type: Memory FoamFirmness: Medium (lighter sleepers will find it medium firm)Height: 10"Trial period: 100 nightsWarranty: 10 yearsPrice: From $179.99 at Novilla

The mattress' one big failing, though, is temperature regulation. I sleep cold so this wasn't an issue, but my husband found it stuffy and, while he didn't wake up sweaty, he didn’t find it massively comfortable either. Hot sleepers on a budget might be happier on the Siena 10" Signature mattress, which kept our testers comfortably cool. But value for money is the Novilla Bliss' big selling point and considering its price, I was really impressed overall with the mattress.

Read on for my full assessment of the Novilla Bliss Memory Foam mattress so you can decide if it’s worth investing in.

A queen size Novilla Bliss is listed at $269.99 with a 20% discount from $337.99 on the brand’s own website, while Amazon currently has the price at $269.99. This sale price seems to be fairly set, so here are the MSRPs for each size, plus the usual sale price you can expect to pay:

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Of course, November is one of the best times of the year for mattress sales and we’re seeing some Black Friday deals — a twin size Novilla 8" hybrid mattress is down to $90, for example, and on Amazon the queen size 10" Novilla Bliss has dropped below $210 a couple of times in 2026. So, it’s definitely worth keeping an eye on prices but do remember that, at $269.99 for a queen, the Novilla Bliss is already incredibly well priced.

Benefits differ very slightly depending on where you buy the mattress. On the brand’s own site, you’ll bet a 100-night trial, 10-year warranty and free shipping and returns. Amazon, on the other hand, offers a 90-night easy returns system, manufacturer’s warranty and free shipping and returns.

An extremely affordable all-foam mattress that offers far more support than you’d expect for its price tag, a queen size Novilla Bliss is currently priced at $269.99 on both the brand’s own website and on Amazon. Keep an eye on prices as Black Friday approaches.

I tested the 10" version, but as detailed above, you can buy the Novilla Bliss in a variety of heights. But for this review, I’m concentrating on the middle ground of the 10” version. Starting at the top, there’s a breathable cover with OEKO-TEX certified fabric. This is helpfully removeable and washable — mattress covers that can’t be removed for freshening up are a real bugbear of mine, although I’d obviously recommend that you use a mattress protector anyway.

Underneath this is a layer of cooling memory foam that’s CertiPUR-US certified and contains the brand’s NanoGEL cooling particles, which Novilla says are designed to ‘capture and redirect excess body heat away from the surface’.

Next up is a layer of adaptive cushioning foam that provides comfort and a transition layer to the high-density support foam layer underneath it. This layer provides most of the support and prevents the mattress from sagging.

Underneath this you’ll find the zip to remove the top cover, plus a non-slip fabric to stop the mattress from sliding about on your bed base. Somewhat annoyingly, the mattress doesn’t have handles to help move it about but as it’s all-foam, it’s not impossible to rotate it without them.

As a lightweight sleeper, I rated the Novilla Bliss as a medium-firm mattress but my husband (and additional testers of a heavier build that I asked to try out the mattress) felt it was a medium, albeit a firmer medium. Averaging out scores, I’d probably place the mattress at a 6 out of 10 on the firmness scale.

There’s definitely some ‘squidge’ when you first lie on the mattress, but this is backed up by a decent amount of support from the lower levels. This combination makes it particularly suited for side sleepers. My husband in particular found the mattress instantly comfortable in this sleeping position, but it did take a couple of days for the foams to soften up a little at the shoulders for me — after this, it was extremely comfortable.

Pressure relief around the pressure points was also really good and I didn’t wake up with any symptoms of a dead hip (something that I can be prone to if the mattress is too unyielding).

I wasn’t expecting great things from this mattress when it came to sleeping on my back, as I’ve historically found all-foam mattresses can lack the firmer lumbar support that I find essential. And, when I first lay down on the bed, I did notice a tiny amount of pulling through my lower back. However, this eased quickly and as a lightweight sleeper, I actually found the mattress supportive enough to keep my spine aligned.

My husband, who boarders the lightweight and average weight category also found it pretty supportive. It’s not going to rival the very best mattresses for back pain but, overall, I thought it did an excellent job on pressure relief for both side and back sleeping.

If you’re of a heavier weight though, I don’t think you’ll find the Novilla Bliss supportive enough and even average weight sleepers towards the higher end of that weight bracket may find it lacks support for back sleeping. I asked a couple of friends who are larger than my husband and I to try the mattress out and while they both thought they could just about get away with it for side sleeping, they felt that support was lacking for both back and stomach sleeping.

In fact, strict stomach sleepers of any weight probably won’t get on with the Novilla Bliss as it’s just lacking in enough support to keep the hips lifted, leading to the spine sinking out of alignment. If you’re a stomach sleeper, have a look at our recommended mattresses for stomach sleepers instead.

I’m in the UK so the mattress was shipped over the Atlantic and, despite its long journey, it arrived none the worse for its voyage. Order on the Novilla website and you’ll receive a tracking number within two business days, with delivery within three to seven business days. Novilla uses FedEx, UPS and GOFO Express for delivery. If you order through Amazon, you can expect delivery in around five days and there’s also the option to pay for the delivery drivers to unpack the mattress and take away packaging.

I recruited my long-suffering husband to help get the mattress upstairs although, being all-foam, it was considerably lighter than the hybrid and pocket sprung mattresses I’ve tested in the past.

Once released from its vacuum seal, the Novilla Bliss did take longer than a hybrid mattress to inflate and I left it for a good 10 hours before sleeping on it. It did definitely continue to expand minutely over the next few days, so I’d say it was around 48 hours before it was fully expanded. The brand suggests that it will take 24-72 hours to fully expand, so this was bang on the money. Some Amazon customers have reported issues with the mattress not expanding fully but in fairness, I didn’t have any issues on this front.

Like most foam mattresses, there was some off-gassing from the Novilla Bliss. It wasn’t the worst I’ve come across but it did last for a couple of days.

My husband and I slept on the mattress for four weeks to get a clear overview of how it performed in key areas. In addition, I carried out some objective tests in an approximation of our comprehensive sleep lab testing methodology.

Through both objective and subjective testing, I’ve assessed the mattress in three key areas. I’ve looked at motion isolation (will a partner moving about at night disturb you?), temperature regulation (does the mattress keep a hot sleeper comfortable through the night?) and edge support (how solid does the edge of the bed feel when you lie right on it or sit on the mattress?). These are the results.

If you share your bed with a restless partner or are a light sleeper, a mattress with good motion isolation is a must. Good motion isolation stops movement from one side of the bed travelling over and waking up another sleeper. I can report back that the Novilla Bliss is particularly strong in this department.

My husband does tend to flail about in bed when he’s rolling over, channeling a walrus trying to leave the ocean and I’m a pretty light sleeper, so even a little motion transfer can be enough to wake me up. I’m pleased to report that I wasn’t disturbed by him at all during our testing period, which was an unusual and pleasing thing.

This was backed up by my objective tests. Firstly, I performed a series of drop tests. I placed a wine glass on the left-hand side of the mattress and dropped a weight from 24" above the bed surface on the right-hand side. This is a similar sensation to a person getting into bed.

I dropped the weight five times consecutively 30" away from the wine glass. Each time, the wine glass gave a very slight wobble but otherwise stayed upright, which was impressive. Next up, I got my husband to perform some subjective tests, starting with low force movements and then increasing to moderate and high force movements. I rated the mattress 10 out of 10 at low force and nine out of 10 at both moderate and high force. Overall, the Novilla Bliss really excelled when it came to motion isolation.

When I talk about temperature regulation, I’m looking at how well the mattress manages heat build-up throughout the night and whether it leaves a sleeper feeling stuffy. I’m afraid this was one area where the Novilla Bliss didn’t perform brilliantly, despite claims of a breathable cover and gel-infused memory foam.

My husband sleeps hot and he found the mattress stuffy after only 15 minutes of lying on it. And while he didn’t wake up seriously overheating, he did feel slightly clammy and uncomfortable. It was not a particularly breathable mattress and, on some hotter nights during testing, he did actually decamp to our spare room.

I’m something of a reptile at the best of times but even I noticed some heat building up around my lower back while lying on it. However, thanks to my cold nature, I wasn’t ever uncomfortable on it.

We tested through the tail end of an unusually warm period in the UK and through to some slightly cooler nights, so it gave me a good overall view of the mattress. For context, temperatures in the room ranged from around 75F down to 60F. However, I should point out that I wouldn’t expect an all-foam mattress to perform as well as a hybrid for temperature regulation and, if you are a hot sleeper, you’d be better off investing in one of our best cooling mattress picks.

A mattress with good edge support allows sleepers to use the whole width of the bed, as well as providing a stable surface to sit on while getting in and out of bed. My husband and I foster cats for a local charity and, as any cat servant will tell you, these little furry creatures have the ability to take up 90% of the bed overnight, leaving human subjects very much clinging to the edges.

Unfortunately, the Novilla Bliss wasn’t the strongest candidate when it came to edge support. There was some definite tilting when we lay on the edges, although I didn’t feel as if I’d actually fall off. It was a similar story when sitting on the edge of the bed — there was some definite tilting, but I didn’t feel as if I’d actually slip off.

To back up my experiences, I placed a 53lb weight midway across and 3" in from the foot and sides of the mattress. The weight sunk in by 5" immediately and dropped further to 6.5" after five minutes. And I had to get my husband to hold the weight the whole time (he only took his hands off very briefly for a photograph).

I repeated this test midway down and 3" in from the side of the mattress and got exactly the same results, with the weight needing to be held the whole time. Just for context, the same weight placed in the center of the mattress compressed by 5" immediately but then didn’t drop any further.

The Novilla Bliss receives overwhelmingly positive reviews from sleepers on both Amazon and the brand’s website. There’s lots of praise for the “exceptional” price and many sleepers praise it for its good quality. Sleepers also praise the mattress for pressure relief, with one customer describing it as the “perfect balance of softness and support…I woke up feeling much more rested without the usual aches and stiffness.” Overall, this is a recurrent theme, along with frequent praise for the motion isolation.

There are nearly 45,000 reviews for the mattress on Amazon so, as you might expect, you will find some complaints in there. The most common one seems to be poor expansion of the mattress, so it would seem that this might be something you’ll need to look out for. And, while many people praise the mattress for soothing aches and pains, stomach sleepers and those of a heavier build complain that the mattress is nowhere near supportive enough for their sleeping style or body weight.

✅ You’re a side sleeper of light or average weight: The Novilla Bliss excelled in pressure relief and comfort for side sleepers, easing tension and providing enough support for a really comfortable night’s sleep.

✅ You share your bed with a restless partner: There really wasn’t any motion transfer to speak of with the Novilla Bliss and I never felt disturbed by my husband moving about.✅ You’re on a budget: At $269.99 for a queen size, the Novilla Bliss is exceptionally good value for money and holds its own against some more expensive options.

❌You sleep on your stomach or are of a heavier build: The all-foam construction of the Novilla Bliss simply isn’t supportive enough for stomach sleepers or those who weigh over 230lbs. Try the Siena Signature mattress instead if you’re on a budget and fall into these categories.❌You’re a hot sleeper: The Novilla Bliss left my hot-sleeping husband feeling pretty stuffy and uncomfortable and its all-foam construction does trap heat a little too easily. The SweetNight CoolNest Memory Foam mattress offers excellent temperature regulation and is another budget option. ❌You need excellent edge support: The Novilla Bliss suffered with some sinkage at its edges and didn’t feel like the most secure surface to lie on the edge of or sit on. If you need an affordable mattress with decent edge support, check out the EGOHOME Black 12” Memory Foam mattress instead.

There are plenty of positives about the Novilla Bliss, but the price is the overwhelming winner. At under $300 for a queen, it’s a bit of a bargain and I was impressed by how well it performed considering that price tag. It certainly beats out quite a few more expensive mattresses when it comes to side sleeping in particular. The soft foams at the top and some decent support underneath mean that this is a great option for side sleepers, except for those of a heavier weight.

It also boasts some of the best motion isolation I’ve come across, and it will be a winner for co-sleepers thanks to this. But, as mentioned, I don’t think it’s a great fit for hot sleepers and I would like to see better edge support.

But overall, I was hugely impressed with this mattress, and I think that most lightweight and average side and back sleepers will be comfortable on this mattress.

This plush pillow is available in two sizes and two different firmness options. In our SquishPillow review, our tester found it best suited to side sleepers, which will match well with the Novilla Bliss. It's also only $29.99, so a bit of a bargain.

Rated the best bed sheets for hot sleepers by our bedding testers, these sheets are silky-soft and cool-to-touch — so they could help to make the Novilla Bliss a bit cooler to sleep on. And there are over a dozen colors/patterns to choose from.

Another way to help make a mattress cooler is to add a cooling mattress topper. The Lucid Gel Memory Foam mattress topper did a great job of keeping our tester cool and it's reasonably priced for such a nice thick topper. A thinner and cheaper 2" version could also save you some money.

When natural light isn't available, the best sunrise alarm clocks are the next best thing. You won't get a better gadget than the Hatch Restore 3 for this and, although it's not the cheapest purchase, it could really help to keep you happy through the winter months.

The best cheap option in our best weighted blankets round up, the YNM Original Cotton Weighted Blanket has a big choice of weights and lots of different colours to choose from - many of which are often dramatically reduced on Amazon.

Jo Plumridge is an experienced mattress reviewer with several years' experience covering all things mattresses and sleep, and who tests memory foam, hybrid and organic mattresses. What Jo doesn't know about a boxed mattress isn't worth knowing, so naturally we tasked her with producing a series of features for Tom's Guide looking at all aspects of mattresses, from how to pick between latex and memory foam (it's a tricky one), to the seven mistakes people make when buying a mattress for the first time. When testing the DreamCloud Luxury Hybrid for Tom's Guide, Jo said: "I loved the back support and pressure relief it offered. Plus, it looks far more expensive than it is." When she isn’t writing about sleep, Jo also writes extensively on interior design, home products and photography.

#3536. 3 Best New Prime Video Series To Binge-Watch This Weekend (November 20–22, 2026)

The 3 best new Prime Video series to binge-watch this weekend, November 20–22, 2026, are an epic fantasy, a historical drama, and a romantic thriller. Prime Video currently has plenty of great streaming options across all genres to dive into this weekend, including major franchises like The Terminal List and Reacher to fan-favorite coming-of-age dramas such as Campus Drivers and Off Campus.

That said, the following three series are the most binge-worthy options on Prime Video right now, all of which are currently dropping new episodes. If you're looking for even more new shows to stream, check out ScreenRant's weekend binge guides for Netflix, Paramount+, and HBO Max, bringing you the latest and greatest choices across these major platforms to take the stress out of streaming this weekend.

The popular romantic K-drama series Love in Disguise is nearing the end of its season 1 run with its finale episode set to arrive on Tuesday, November 24. The 12-part series premiered back in mid-October and has been one of the most viral new releases on Prime Video this Fall 2026, currently ranking #3 on its worldwide viewership chart. Love in Disguise is celebrated for its high entertainment value and outstanding performances from its lead actors, who, according to audiences, have undeniable and infectious on-screen chemistry.

Love in Disguise follows a developing love story between a wealthy businessman and his new secretary, although his employee is much more than meets the eye. Once a special forces officer, she is now secretly working undercover to investigate a murder case in which her boss is a suspect. What's more, the covert secretary is also disguised as a man, revealing a repressed sexual interest within her boss. Now is the perfect time to binge the available 10 episodes of Love in Disguise before its final two episodes land early next week.

The Chosen is once again one of the top trending series on Prime Video worldwide following its season 6 premiere last Sunday, November 15. The Chosen season 6 chronicles one of the darkest eras of Jesus' life during his final 24 hours. The fan-favorite series has already been renewed for a seventh and final season.

The Chosen is currently #2 on Prime Video's U.S. streaming chart and sixth worldwide, indicating that the long-running biblical series still has momentum since its 2019 debut. The series also earned a near-perfect 97% Rotten Tomatoes audience score and a remarkably high 9.1 IMDb score, placing it just outside IMDb's Top 50 TV shows of all time. The epic high-fantasy series is the #1 most-watched Prime Video series in the world and has already been confirmed for a fourth season.

Disney's 8-part supernatural fantasy epic returns this Friday with a highly anticipated new chapter featuring Greek gods, monsters, and an epic quest.

With just two episodes remaining in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, there has never been a better time to press play on the series than right now, even if you have yet to watch the first two seasons.
