#3535. 10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?)

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

An isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

The Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

One of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

If you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

If you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it big and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for new planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

Want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

If you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous new reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

If you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend says a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.

#3530. Forget ‘Landman,’ Billy Bob Thornton’s Forgotten Matt Damon Western Is Officially a Netflix Hit

Billy Bob Thornton is experiencing a major career renaissance thanks to his role as Tommy Norris in Taylor Sheridan's Western series, Landman. To older generations, the multi-hyphenate might be better recognized for his rise to stardom in the mid-90s, which culminated in his big-screen success in the aughties. Though he's found more success as an actor, Thornton's filmmaking skills are, in fact, responsible for his first thrust into the limelight. Thornton wrote, directed, and starred in his breakthrough feature, the Academy Award-winning Southern Gothic drama Sling Blade, released in 1996.

After Sling Blade's success, Thornton would make a few more directorial efforts, but unfortunately, none were quite as successful. His next credit as director was Daddy and Me, which, though sharing a similar theme as Sling Blade, didn't get a major release. Up next was All the Pretty Horses, an adaptation of Cormac McCarthy's beloved novel of the same name released in 2000. Though the Western film, starring Matt Damon opposite Penélope Cruz, did get a major theatrical release, it was marred by behind-the-scenes conflicts, including then-Miramax boss Harvey Weinstein's controversial decision to drastically cutthe runtime against Thornton's wishes.

All the Pretty Horses would consequently be released to box office failure, grossing only $18.1 million against its hefty $57 million production budget. It was also a critical disaster, deemed "flat" and "uninvolving" compared to the novel, and is barely spoken about these days. However, Netflix recently licensed it for multiple international territories, and surprisingly, it is charting in several of those countries. Unfortunately, it appears to be unavailable on Netflix US, though it can be accessed in the US via major PVOD channels.

The show that claimed the most of your answers is the world you were built for. If two tied, both are shown — you're complicated enough to straddle two Sheridan universes.

You are a Dutton — or you might as well be. You understand that some things are worth protecting at any cost, and that the modern world's indifference to history, to land, to legacy, is not something you're willing to accept quietly. You lead from the front, you carry your family's weight without complaint, and when someone threatens what's yours, you don't escalate — you finish it. You're not cruel. But you are absolute. In Yellowstone's world, that combination of ferocity and loyalty doesn't make you a villain. It makes you the only thing standing between everything that matters and everyone who wants to take it.

You thrive in the chaos of high-stakes negotiation, where the money is enormous, the margins are thin, and the wrong word in the wrong room can cost everyone everything. You're a fixer — the person called when a situation is already on fire and needs someone with the nerve to walk into it. West Texas oil country rewards exactly what you are: sharp, adaptable, unsentimental, and absolutely clear-eyed about what people want and what they'll do to get it. You're not naive enough to think this world is fair. You're smart enough to be the one deciding who it's fair to.

You are a Dwight Manfredi — someone who has served their time, paid their dues, and arrived somewhere unexpected with nothing but their reputation and their wits. You adapt without losing yourself. You build loyalty through respect rather than fear, though you're not above reminding people that the two aren't mutually exclusive. Tulsa King is for people who are still standing when everyone assumed they'd be finished — who find, in an unfamiliar place, that they're more capable than the world gave them credit for. You don't need a throne. You build one, wherever you happen to land.

You carry the weight of a system that is broken by design, and you do it anyway — because someone has to, and because you're the only one positioned to do it without the whole thing collapsing. Mike McLusky's world is for people who are comfortable operating where there are no good options, only less catastrophic ones. You speak every language: law enforcement, criminal, political, human. That fluency makes you invaluable and it makes you a target. You've made your peace with both. Mayor of Kingstown belongs to people who understand that keeping the peace is not the same as being at peace — and who do the job regardless.

All the Pretty Horses' poor critical reception was a sharp contrast to actor Matt Damon's sentiments. Damon once called it "the best thing I've ever been a part of"; however, he was referring to Thornton's director's cut, which was 3 hours and 40 minutes. "You can't cut 35% of the movie and expect it to be the same movie,” he once argued. Given that much of the film's criticisms (pacing, incoherence) could be a consequence of its edited runtime, it's safe to say that the marketing essentially botched what should've otherwise been a good film.

Thornton keeps a copy of the cut and, during a 2022 interview with Collider, revealed his wish to have it released someday, should he manage to navigate the complicated rights issues involved. #3529. DC Shares Official Image Of New Robin, Answering Burning Fan Question

DC just shared a new image of its latest iteration of Robin, answering a major fan question about this new hero's superpowers. Here's the new art, and everything we know about the latest Boy Wonder.

DC recently rebooted the iconic Legion of Super-Heroes - a group of superhumans from the 31st Century, inspired to found a new 'Age of Heroes' by the legacy of the modern day Superman. With Brainiac hunting different versions of the Legion across the multiverse, they find themselves beset by an enemy they can't comprehend.

DC recently announced the latest recruit to the Legion would be Bat-Lad - a future version of Robin who follows Batman's legacy rather than the Man of Steel's. The first art of the character raised questions about his powers that DC has just answered.

DC recently revealed V. Ken Marion's cover for Legion of Super-Heroes #4, showing Bat-Lad in action. The young hero is shown in a dingy street with a shadowy being behind him. This is something fans already saw in Hayden Sherman and Tamra Bonvillain's main cover (below), but it far more clearly communicates the new hero's powers.

While that cover showed a silhouette behind Bat-Lad, Marion's art makes it clear that the shadow is a physical being controlled by Bat-Lad, with its Venom-like ichor curling around his arm. It's also clear that the original cover isn't obscuring this shadow being - the all-black appearance is its official design.

The new cover appears to confirm that Bat-Lad is essentially a reverse-Robin. While the original Robin is Batman's sidekick, Bat-Lad appears to be able to summon a towering creature of living darkness. It's an awesome twist on the 'Batman and Robin' partnership, showing how Batman's legacy has been warped over the centuries.

Sadly, it seems that Bat-Lad's powers have a major drawback, as the summary for the issue tells fans to "Welcome a boy and his uncontrollable shadow monster to the world of Legion!" Despite this, DC refers to Bat-Lad as a "new legionnaire," confirming he'll join the team.

Fans don't yet know much about Bat-Lad other than that he dresses in Robin's colors and can summon a shadow monster. However, it's possible he comes from Planet Gotham. This location was introduced in 2020's Legion of Super-Heroes, characterized as the galaxy's first artificially created planet.

Planet Gotham echoes Batman's iconic city, with a noir aesthetic and ruled over by a president referred to as the 'Commissioner.' The populace are served by robots using the holographic visage of Bruce Wayne's butler Alfred Pennyworth and policed by androids in the style of Victorian 'bobbies.'

Planet Gotham is characterized as an essentially crime-free utopia, but one with a strict rule of law. Casinos and gaudy luxury are everywhere, suggesting the limits of Batman's ability to truly change Gotham's spirit, no matter the time frame.

DC's 31st Century was canonically rewritten by recent events, so the world of the Legion of Super-Heroes isn't quite as fans remember it. That could mean that Planet Gotham no longer exists, however with each Legionnaire tending to be from a different planet, so it would make a lot of sense for Bat-Lad to call Planet Gotham home.

The Legion of Super-Heroes are known for having a massive membership, making even the Justice League at its height look small. Each era adds a few new heroes, often as commentary on DC lore at the time or on modern-day themes.

The last major addition to the team was the mysterious Gold Lantern, who became an object of fascination for fans and built on the idea of the multi-colored Lantern Corps. Now, the Robin of the 3st Century is set to join the team, as Bat-Lad heads towards his debut.

Legion of Super-Heroes #4 is coming December 9 from DC Comics.

#3528. The Best Early Black Friday Deals on DeWalt, Milwaukee, and Ryobi Cordless Power Tools

Becca Lewis is home maintenance writer who aims to foster confidence in and inspire DIY enthusiasts at all skill levels.

Becca attended Southern Connecticut State University, where she studied technical theater and design. She has a background in carpentry and fabrication and has worked in specialty shops, using a wide variety of tools and materials, for more than 20 years.

Becca has also written for Angi, where she specializes in creating guides for DIY, home maintenance, and renovations, and she indulges her love of sci-fi and fantasy by writing about entertainment and science for Giant Freakin Robot. She serves on the board of the Good Junk Sanctuary in Portland, Oregon, focusing on community engagement in the DIY and reuse space.

If you have a DIY enthusiast on your list—or if you just want some new tools for your own projects—Black Friday sales are a good time to snag low prices on quality tools. Lots of big box stores are looking to thin out their inventory and make room for next year’s upgrades, so in addition to encouraging a holiday rush, retailers are motivated to price things to move. If you know what to look for, you can get up to 65% off on trusted brands. Here are a few of the best deals out there right now.

If you’re building a new cordless tool set, or updating your battery system, getting a cordless tool set can save you some money because these combos usually include batteries and a charger, which can be the most expensive part of your tool set. Here are a few of the best early Black Friday deals on cordless tool sets.

The Ryobi 6-tool 18-volt combo set is on sale for $199, 33% off its regular price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, a circular saw, a sawzall, an oscillating multi-tool, a work light, a 1.5-amp-hour battery, a 4-amp-hour battery, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted home tool brand.

The Ryobi 18-volt drill and driver set is on sale for $99, 34% off its usual price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, two 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a great starter set because it has the first two tools you need for a cordless kit and it comes with batteries so you can expand your set for cheaper as you develop your skills.

The Ryobi 4-tool, 4-volt project set is on sale for $99, 61% off its typical price at Home Depot. This set comes with a rotary tool, a project light, a glue pen, a mini drill, two rechargeable batteries, a charging cable, a set of starter rotary bits, and three glue sticks. This set is handy for DIY projects that require fine detail, like wood carving, craft projects, or framing pictures.

The DeWalt drill and driver combo set is on sale for $149, 38% off its regular price on Amazon. This set includes a drill, an impact driver, 2 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted brand for drills and drivers, and a good start for a cordless DIY tool set.

If you have a cordless tool set already and you want to expand your kit, or if you have a DIYer in your life who already has a particular brand of battery and you want to get them something they can use, a single tool deal can be just the thing.

The DeWalt cordless 20-volt cutout saw is on sale on Amazon for $102.95, 53% off its typical price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a 20-volt DeWalt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for custom trimming drywall, cutting custom shapes for going around outlet covers, or custom cutting trim in tight spaces.

The DeWalt 20-volt cordless angle grinder is on sale at Lowe’s for $209, 47% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a 4-amp-hour battery, but you’ll need a DeWalt 20-volt charger to use it. This is a good tool for metalworking or for grinding down screw tips that poke through or trimming bolt ends off.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact drill/driver is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. It’s a good first tool for a set.

The Milwaukee 18-volt impact wrench is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 68% off its typical price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. This is a good tool for driving bolts through tough materials and for automotive projects.

The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multi-tool is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 50% off its regular price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it's ready to use out of the box. This is one of the most versatile cordless tools, allowing you to cut a wide range of materials and use a sanding attachment to do finishing work as well.

The Milwaukee 18-volt tire inflator kit is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 65% off its usual price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to go right out of the box. This is an excellent addition to your emergency roadside tool set because you can use it to inflate a car tire with the charged 18-volt batteries.

The Makita 18-volt cordless electric 2-inch brad nailer is on sale on Amazon for $324, 38% off its regular price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a Makita 18-volt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for attaching trim or paneling.

Yes, Home Depot has already launched its early Black Friday deals, offering deep discounts on major brands of cordless power tools. They also update their sales page on Thanksgiving Day and include Black Friday in-store-only doorbusters as part of their seasonal sales.

For most home tool sets, Ryobi is a solid, durable, and versatile brand. If you plan to use your tools occasionally for home maintenance, this is the best bang for your buck. For daily use or for larger DIY projects, DeWalt tends to be the next best option. These tools have more robust chargers and tend to stand up to more rigorous use than Ryobi tools.

If you’re building a new cordless tool set or updating your battery system, getting a cordless tool set can save you money because these combos usually include batteries and a charger, which can be the most expensive part of your tool set. If you already have a cordless tool set and you want to expand your kit, or if you have a DIYer in your life who already has a particular brand of battery and you want to get them something else they can use, a single tool deal might make more sense.

#3527. Kentucky Mom Charged With Incest Being Heavily Monitored In Jail, Officials Say

The Kentucky mom of three charged with incest for repeatedly having sex with an 11-year-old boy is being watched like a hawk by security cameras and correctional officers while she's in jail ... TMZ has learned.

Larue County Jailer Jody Perry tells TMZ ... Lauren Winans is sharing a small cell with 2 other female inmates in the women's dormitory of the Larue County Jail. Perry says the 3 women are the only females currently incarcerated at the jail, and they are being monitored 24/7 by the security cameras, with officers doing cell checks every 15 to 20 minutes.

Therefore, Perry says, Lauren won't be able to engage in any naughty behavior like fighting or fornicating with her cellmates ... and if they see anything questionable, they will "put a stop to it."

Perry also says that given her charges, Lauren would have been placed in the sex offender dormitory, which is a segregation unit, if she were a man. But because men are more violent than women, Perry says, there's no chance that he would allow Lauren to cohabitate with men in a cell.

As for whether Lauren can have conjugal visits with her husband -- Bardstown police officer Andy Winans -- Perry says hell no! Perry says he doesn't give a "rat's ass" if the husband is President of the United States ... there will be no special privileges for cops!

In addition, Perry says Lauren gets 3 squares a day, and what's on the menu is your average American fare ... such as pancakes, biscuits and gravy, cinnamon rolls, eggs, potatoes, sausage, pasta, stir-fry, and rice meals.

After a big meal, Perry says Lauren can go to recreation for one hour each day and play cornhole, handball, and even do chin-ups using a chin-up bar.

She's also allowed video visitation at a kiosk in the jail, and she can even kick back and watch cable TV in her cell.

As we reported ... prosecutors have charged Lauren with first-degree sodomy, incest, and sexual abuse involving a child under age 12. Lauren has pleaded not guilty to the charges and is being held on $250,000 bond in the county jail.

Lauren allegedly sexually abused an 11-year-old boy on 3 separate occasions, groping him twice and engaging in "oral abuse" once. A police detective testified in court that the alleged victim told cops Lauren told him the alleged abuse was "normal."

Amazon's early Black Friday sale is bringing some pretty significant discounts on Apple devices, including several of the company's latest releases. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

The Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) is down to $329 from $399, saving you $70. If you'd prefer to occasionally leave your iPhone behind, the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS + Cellular, 42mm) is $70 off, bringing its price down to $429 from $499. For a more affordable option, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) is down to $199 from $249, saving you $50. Check out PCMag's review for a closer look at what you get for the price.

The Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS + Cellular, 40mm) is also $50 off, bringing its price down to $249 from $299. For an extra $50 over the GPS-only model, you get the convenience of making calls, sending messages, and staying connected without keeping your iPhone nearby, provided you have an active cellular plan. It's worth considering if you regularly go for runs, head to the gym, or step out without your phone but still want to stay reachable.

You still get the M5 chip, faster SSD performance, and Wi-Fi 7 support, all in a smaller, lighter design.

#3524. 10 Shows Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

While families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other shows mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

Another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's company town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the new sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

MobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates new maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Company all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

Best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other shows on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

The great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a new adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

#3523. Nick Cannon Asks For Prayers From Hospital Bed Before Lupus Treatment

Nick Cannon is asking fans for prayers from a hospital bed before heading into a scanning procedure that's part of his lupus treatment.

The "Wild 'N Out" host shared a photo of him in a hospital bed wearing a face mask, writing across the snap ... "This [world] can definitely take a lot out of you. Pray for me y'all."

He also added the hashtag "Lupus Warrior" in the caption.

#3522. 6 Western Movies From the ’90s That Are 10/10 Masterpieces

There's nothing quite like a good Western. Although the golden age of the horse opera was undoubtedly the mid-20th century, the genre continued to persevere long afterward. In fact, there was a Western renaissance in the 1990s that took Hollywood — and the Academy Awards — by storm. From genre staples like Clint Eastwood and Kevin Costner to visionary filmmakers like Ang Lee and Richard Donner, the '90s sparked new life into the Old West.

Whether you prefer comedic takes on the genre, action-packed shoot-'em-ups, or deconstructive takes that raise the Western from the ground up, there's something here for everyone. Outlaws, lawmen, soldiers, and cowboys galore make up some of the greatest thrills of the '90s centered entirely on the American West. Whether you adore these flicks already or have yet to visit them, these are some of the decade's greatest Westerns — so don't sleep on them.

Starting this list off with perhaps the most controversial pick, Young Guns II deserves its place in the Western canon. A high-octane sequel to the original 1988 flick, the Emilio Estevez-led Billy the Kid action romp pits the Regulators against the lawman Pat Garrett (William Petersen), who aims to bring Billy and his friends in on several outstanding warrants. The result is an intense cat-and-mouse ride across the New Mexican desert, and it's a blast for those who haven't had the pleasure.

Young Guns II is arguably even greater than its predecessor. Billy, Doc (Kiefer Sutherland), Chavez (Lou Diamond Phillips), and the rest of the Regulators carry the weight of the picture with their trademark charm and "Brat Pack" pull. The fast-pulling sequel does everything it can to surpass the original, armed with a killer Jon Bon Jovi theme and plenty of fabulous performances that deserve high praise. There's a reason that folks are still calling for a third entry after all these years — and long after the fates of the Regulators have already been met.

The Wild West era and the American Civil War are so inexplicably linked that one cannot divorce the Western from the war itself. Director Ang Lee understood this profoundly when tackling Ride with the Devil, a Civil War-era trial by fire that chronicles a group of Missouri Bushwhackers as they battle the Jayhawkers invading their Southern home. Its meditations on the origins of Western violence as an outgrowth from the war itself are quite complex, and the picture pulls no punches as it does so. Tobey Maguire and Skeet Ulrich star as childhood friends Jake Roedel and Jack Bull Chiles seek revenge on those who threatened their home.

Like many Westerns, Ride with the Devil offers a nuanced take on the war that explores the evils of both sides. That said, the Irregulars are portrayed as almost akin to a typical Western outlaw gang. Jake's struggle with the Southern cause, and his growing friendship with former slave Daniel Holt (Jeffrey Wright), is what forges his path as an honorable man. It may not be the first film that comes to mind when you think of the Old West — indeed it's very much rooted in the Civil War itself — but it would be hard to consider the film anything but a Western in style and substance.

Based on the popular Western television program of the same name, Richard Donnor brought Bret Maverick (Mel Gibson) to the big screen with the comedic Maverick. When the titular gambler finds himself in search of the funds to enter a high-stakes poker game, he ventures across the Old West alongside Annabelle Bransford (Jodie Foster) and Marshal Zane Cooper (James Garner), who certainly give him a run for his money. If you loved the show, you'll get a kick out of the big-screen version.

Maverick reminds us, like Young Guns II, that the genre can be fun as much as it is introspective. Gibson plays the unusual Western "hero" with genuine charm and an unassuming con artistry that certainly honors the original series. It's not your typical Western, but that's exactly why it's such a stellar entry. Of course, Maverick turns out to actually be a continuation rather than a straight-up reboot, but the way it reveals such a fact is exactly the sort of slight-of-hand that gives Bret Maverick his edge.

Four icons and four completely different ways of walking into trouble. This is the one you would have been out there, why it fits, and what it would have cost you.

You have never explained yourself and you have never needed to, because people work out fairly quickly that you are the most capable person in the room without you ever having to mention it.

You are the funniest person in most rooms and the most loyal person in all of them, and you would be genuinely insulted if somebody suggested those two things were in any tension.

You never wanted this job, and you took it anyway because the alternative was standing there watching somebody less careful do it badly, which is the most Western reason there has ever been.

Nobody has ever successfully talked you out of something you had already decided was right, and a long line of grown adults has found that out the hard way.

The first Western to win Best Picture at the Oscars in decades, Dances with Wolves was Kevin Costner's directorial debut that proved the Western could be as epic as ever. With a screenplay by Michael Blake based on his novel of the same name, the film follows Lt. John Dunbar as he is stationed out on the American frontier following his heroic (but secretly suicidal) actions during the Civil War. Caught between the Pawnee and Sioux, Dunbar eventually finds himself on the other end of his own country's barrel.

Dances with Wolves is a breathtaking motion picture. It's an introspective glimpse into both the effects of the Civil War and the lives of the Native American peoples who lived on the frontier long before it was settled. More than that, it was a trailblazer in native representation in Hollywood, and though not a true story, is largely based on historical truths. Beyond that, it's also just a great time, as Costner proves himself to be one of the genre's biggest champions.

Is there a more well-known or highly-celebrated '90s Western by audiences and critics alike than Tombstone? The spectacular Kurt Russell-led picture follows former lawman Wyatt Earp, his two brothers, and their friend Doc Holliday (Val Kilmer) as they arrive in the titular Arizona town just in time to square off with the ravenous Cowboys gang. As they do, things go from bad to worse as Tombstone falls into chaos — and the Earps bring hell on their adversaries.

Tombstone does absolutely everything right. It's thrilling, action-packed, and chock-full of some of the best on-screen dialogue in the business. Russell and Kilmer steal the show, but the entire stacked cast more than prove themselves over the course of these fast-moving 130 minutes. It's hard to rank the best performances in Tombstone given how stellar each actor truly is, but we all know that this movie wouldn't work nearly as well without Val Kilmer.

Just two years after Dances with Wolves reminded everyone that the Western still had real life left in it, Unforgiven came in and nabbed that Best Picture Oscar for itself. Directed by Clint Eastwood, the genre star tackles his final on-screen Western as William Munny, an aged former gunslinger who returns for one last job to provide for his family. It's a stellar revisionist picture that does everything right as Eastwood bids the genre that made him a final heartfelt farewell.

It doesn't get much better than Unforgiven. With brilliant performances by Morgan Freeman, Richard Harris, and Gene Hackman, the picture excels in the way it unpacks the genre's most famous tropes and reconstructs them into Eastwood's final dissertation on what makes the Western truly exceptional. There are few Westerns so highly celebrated as Unforgiven, and although Eastwood may best be known for his work on the Dollars Trilogy, there's a reason this won Best Picture.

#3519. Major websites compromised to steal crypto from iPhone users

A security researcher has discovered that some of the world’s most popular websites were compromised in an attempt to steal cryptocurrency from iPhone users.

A total of 178 websites were affected, including BBC, CNN, HSBC, IKEA, and Zoom. Reasonably recent versions of iOS are safe, and so far it appears that only a few thousand dollars have been stolen …

Reuters reports that hackers attacked Optimizely, a website optimization platform used by many major websites.

Several of the affected companies said that they have disabled the Optimizely scripts and are investigating potential impacts. Helme says almost all of the rogue code has now been removed, and that Apple patched iOS after an identical attack method was detected last month.

The Coruna loader is byte-identical to a sample we analysed in October from a different campaign. The kit’s own comments say iOS 18.7.3 and later, and 26.3 and later, are patched.

Helme monitored the attacker’s wallets and discovered that only $7,040 has been stolen, though it’s not possible to see how many payment card numbers were obtained.

As always, the best protection against this type of attack is to promptly update all your Apple devices to the latest OS versions they support.

#3513. How to hide the new macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator

macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override. Apple describes itas a transparency indicator that appears when one app is controlling another.

If you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar. Prefer to hide it? There’s a Terminal workaround.

I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.

Open Terminal and run these two commands:

sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false

Enter your Mac administrator password when prompted, then restart your Mac.

The command disables the internal AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR feature flag. It doesn’t remove apps from your permissions list, although you’ll no longer see this activity indicator.

To restore Apple’s default behavior, run:

sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR

Restart your Mac again to apply the reversal. This removes only the indicator override, preserving any other flags you may have configured.

This is an undocumented workaround tested on the current beta, so Apple could change or remove it in a future update.

Black Friday brings the biggest gaming discounts, and that’s no different this year if you own an Xbox. There’s a slight caveat, though: the consoles — the Xbox Series S and Xbox Series X — aren’t on sale thanks to RAMageddon. That said, you can still save on discounted games and peripherals.

Right now, you can get The Game Awards nominees, like Resident Evil Requiem for $39 at Amazon. Meanwhile, Pragmata is another fantastic Capcom title discounted by $20. Peripherals-wise, the standard Xbox controller is $20 off, while the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X is $99. Finally, you can get a 12-month Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscription for $5 off.

Whether you’re new to Xbox or just want to build out your gaming library, now is the best time to do so. Not only because of Black Friday deals, but also because of the awesome games on the Xbox horizon. Here are the latest Xbox Black Friday deals. I’ll update this post regularly, so be sure to check back for the latest savings!

The Xbox Series S is limited to 1440p output but still delivers fast loading, ray tracing, and high frame rates. It features a GPU with up to 4 teraflops of output, 10GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. This console has no disc drive; it's designed exclusively for digital games.

The Xbox Series X All-Digital is the same powerful console with two key differences. Firstly, it comes in an attractive Robot White hue, and it also lacks a disc drive, so it is designed solely for digital play. It's the perfect console for Xbox Game Pass players.

Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is one of the most memorable entries in the Sonic the Hedgehog series. Packed with chaos, fun, and a bit of a learning curve, CrossWorlds shines with smooth drifting and air tricks that deliver significant boosts.

The latest game in the Mafia series takes you back to 1900s Sicily, the birthplace of organized crime. You play Enzo, a fresh recruit in the Torrisi crime family, and must work your way up the ranks to become a "made man." Offering a narrative-driven campaign packed with third-person firefights and high-speed chases (in cars and on horseback), Mafia: The Old Country is a highly engaging action-adventure game.

Assassin’s Creed Shadows delivers on its promise of bringing back classic stealth mechanics while introducing new ones and combining the best of the older and RPG titles. The detailed open world of feudal Japan feels alive, with compelling playable and non-playable characters, and varied fighting tactics enrich the combat. But the game struggles to balance its two playable protagonists, and player choices are still inconsequential.

Resident Evil Requiem combines elements from prior installments to deliver one of the strongest entries yet. Though it doesn’t take risks, its thrilling gameplay and stunning graphics keep you engaged from beginning to end.

Pragmata is a breath of fresh air thanks to its tactical combat, clever puzzles, and earnest sci-fi story. It proves that there's still innovation in the AAA space and is yet another winner from Capcom. This is a game that humans and androids alike can enjoy.

Star Wars Zero Company is a new turn-based tactics game where you recruit and lead a squad of operators and experience an original Star Wars story set during the Clone Wars. Offering strategic combat, cinematic production values, and a focus on player decisions, it's one of the best Star Wars video games in ages and a potential GOTY pick.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes everything folks know about Batman from popular culture and filters it through the tried-and-true Lego formula. Whether you're a fan of Batman or Lego games, there's a lot to love in this charming adventure.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor with a larger scope, both narratively and in gameplay. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer deep customization. Aside from some confusing maps, this is an almost perfect action-based title.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark, brilliantly written vampire RPG with a superb prologue, a memorable cast, and inventive powers. Repetitive combat, a rough performance, and an insipid lead drag it down at times. A flawed, fascinating debut with cult classic written all over it — one that needs some post-launch patches, but kept us hooked regardless.

Step into the cockpit, take flight, and prepare for battle in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, the latest installment in the popular aerial combat franchise. Boasting a full single-player campaign and the series largest suite of online modes to date, not to mention stunning visuals and sound, it's the complete Ace Combat package.

007 First Light is the finest James Bond video game in nearly 30 years. Its cinematic single-player campaign is remarkable, delivering a gripping, quintessentially Bond story paired with some of the best action-adventure set pieces we’ve ever experienced. Whether you’re a longtime Bond fan or a newcomer, 007 First Light is unmissable.

Crimson Desert is one of the most ambitious single-player open-world games ever. It throws a ton of deep systems at you with almost no hand-holding, but once it clicks, the combat feels fantastic, and exploration feels rewarding. There’s enough content here to keep you busy for months on end. The story is pretty average, and the beginning can be brutal, but if you love big sandbox adventures, this one is worth the ride (and $69).

Versatile, comfortable, and responsive, the Xbox Core Wireless Controller impressed us in our rigorous testing. This isn't just for Xbox — it's compatible with PC, Android, and iOS devices too. With its ergonomic design, textured grips, and a button to share screenshots with friends, it's a go-to for gamers everywhere.

The Arctis Nova 5 is one of the finest gaming headsets, and it's the highest-scoring headset we've reviewed. Compatible with PS5, Nintendo Switch, PC, Android, iOS and Meta Quest, its quick-switch 2.4GHz dongle and Bluetooth 5.3 enable you to effortlessly swap between devices. The sound quality is incredible, and the 360° spatial audio makes your gaming experiences even more immersive.

The Nacon Revolution X Unlimited Controller is a high-end pad designed for the Xbox Series consoles and PC. It packs pro features like hall effect sticks, adjustable triggers, mappable back buttons, a customizable LC screen, and a rechargeable battery. At $199, it's not a cheap investment, but if you take your Xbox gaming seriously, it's a worthwhile upgrade.

#3511. Kentucky Mom Charged With Incest is Heavy Drinker Who Dates Cops, Exes Say

The Kentucky mom charged with sexually abusing her 11-year-old son has a history of dating cops and heavy drinking ... at least according to her exes.

According to court documents obtained by The Post, Lauren Winans' baby daddies Daniel Newton and Derrick Carrico raised concerns that Lauren abuses alcohol and has "been with at least 16 different local deputies and police officers."

In a 2024 affidavit filed in his custody battle over their 9-year-old son, Newton wrote ... "Unfortunately, Lauren jumps from man to man."

Newton said "her children have been exposed to at least nine different men in Lauren's life" since her 2022 divorce from Carrico.

In his own filing for custody, Carrico claims Lauren brought their daughter over to now-husband Andy Winans' house for a sleepover in 2024 ... just one day after he'd signed an agreement with his ex-wife.

According to Carrico's affidavit, Lauren took her daughter to Andy's around 11 PM, and the little girl later told him ... "I want to tell you something, but I was told not to tell you, Nana, or Papa."

Carrico claimed ... "The child informed me that … she was made to sleep in the bed with her mom and the other man."

While that's disturbing enough on its own, Lauren and Andy got married about 3 weeks after his divorce from his ex was finalized.

Between this and her alleged alcohol abuse, the judge made both Newton and Carrico the primary residential caretakers of their kids.

The judge said her alleged drinking and mental health issues were "the biggest issue clearly before this court," but also stressed that it was also troubling how she decided to "hastily uproot her children from their maternal grandparents' residence and to require them to basically live with strangers (Andy and his three children)."

As you know, Lauren has recently been charged with first-degree sodomy, incest, and sexual abuse involving a child under age 12 ... for allegedly abusing her oldest son.

The charges come after the boy told his stepmom that his mom allegedly assaulted him on three separate occasions in 2022 ... when he was just 11 years old.

During Lauren's bond hearing Thursday, a detective testified that his investigation uncovered three alleged incidents of sexual abuse ... claiming she allegedly groped the boy twice and once engaged in "oral abuse."

The detective alleged that Lauren's son told her to stop during the third incident, but she told him the alleged abuse was "normal."

Lauren has pleaded not guilty to the charges and is being held on $250,000 bond in the county jail, where she's being closely monitored.

#3509. Now These Apple Services Are Down

If you're having trouble accessing certain Apple products and services today, you are not alone. As of early Tuesday afternoon, Downdetector shows user reports of issues across multiple Apple services. While Apple's System Status page initially showed far fewer issues than Downdetector users reported, the site has since updated to reflect general outages.

According to users on Downdetector, there are currently outages or interruptions to the following Apple services, in order of most to least reported: Apple Support, Apple Pay, iCloud, App Store, Apple Business Manager, Apple Music, Apple Store, Sign In with Apple, Apple Card. As of 1:44 p.m., Apple Support had the most reports, with over 13,000 user complaints. Comments suggest that users cannot log into their iCloud accounts, Apple Accounts, or activate devices, among other issues.

According to Apple, the disruptions aren't quite as widespread: Apple says that the App Store, Apple Music, AppleCare on Devices, and Schoolwork are all experiencing outages. Apple says that the App Store and Apple Music "may be slow or unavailable," while AppleCare purchase is currently unavailable. The company's System Status page shows an "issue" with iCloud Account & Sign In. Other services with user reports on Downdetector, including the Apple Card, Apple Online Store, and Apple Business, read as "Available." Apple also says there was an outage with the Volume Purchase Program, but that has since been resolved.

It's not clear what's causing the issues with the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud Account & Sign In, or other Apple services at this time. However, the timing is odd. It comes after a number of banks experienced outages on Monday, as well as Microsoft's massive outage the previous week. In addition to all of these outages, the FAA unexpectedly grounded all U.S. flights on Friday, for only the third time in the agency's history.

#3508. iOS 27.3 will give iCloud+ subscribers two new perks

When iOS 27.3 beta 2 debuted earlier this week, we detailed how the update introduces AI usage limits for Siri AI and select other features.

For AI features that depend on server-based models, each device running iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, or macOS 27.3 will have limited daily access to advanced AI features. These include complex Siri AI requests, Image Playground, certain Photos app editing tools, and more.

The only iCloud+ tier that doesn’t include higher limits is the $0.99/month plan.

Read more: Apple reveals how iCloud+ increases Siri AI and Apple Intelligence usage limits

In the Shortcuts app, the ‘Use Model’ action lets you choose between a few different model options, including Cloud, Cloud Pro, On-Device, and ChatGPT.

People should at least have the 200 GB model. When I worked at The Apple Store (Did Retail and Corporate) I always recommended iCloud, and highlighted the backup feature. I can’t tell you the amount of people who lost or got their phones damaged / destroyed and lost precious photos, videos that they could never get back. Nearly all signed up.

I did offer alternatives like backing to your Mac or external SSD, but to have a proper backup safety system you need 1-2 backups at home and one off site (ie. friends house, storage facility, etc.) and you would have to be consistent with your backups and drop offs. Most people don’t have the time so they do iCloud, same as I.

I’m at 2 TB, probably going to 6 TB, cause I love taking photos and videos of special events.

Similar to Apple’s other AI usage limits, your access to the Cloud Pro model in Shortcuts increases if you have a higher storage plan. Per this support document, the 200GB plan supports standard limits, the 2TB plan offers 5x access, followed by 10x on the 6TB plan and 20x on the 12TB plan.

iCloud+ already provided far more than just increased cloud storage, but with iOS 27.3 it’s set to be an asset for AI power users too.

iCloud+ is available as a standalone subscription or through the Apple One bundle, which also includes Apple TV, Apple Music, and more.

#3506. Sarah Michelle Gellar Reveals Surprising Freddie Prinze Jr. Connection

Sarah Michelle Gellar told E! News that through Ancestry, with whom she partnered for its Gathering the Good initiative, she and Freddie Prinze Jr. learned they have a mutual connection to The Bronx.

Now this is a revelation to wig out over.

Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr.’s paths didn’t officially cross until the late ‘90s on I Know What You Did Last Summer, but as they recently learned they had more in common than they realized. Specifically, a shared family experience that traces back decades before they graced the screen.

“We always joke that the closest connection I had to my husband's side of the family,” Gellar told E! News in an exclusive interview, “was that for a small time I went to the same high school that my husband's dad went to, and that was like sort of our one thing.”

After all, though Gellar—mom to Charlotte, 17, and Rocky, 14, with Prinze—is a native New Yorker, her husband was born in Los Angeles and grew up in New Mexico. (His dad Freddie Prinze, however, hailed from New York.)

She continued, “Then through Ancestry, we found out that our grandparents lived less than two miles away from each other in the Bronx at one point, which they could have potentially known each other. That's kind of crazy.”

For the Buffy the Vampire Slayer star, who teamed up with Ancestry for its Gathering the Good initiative, it was an opportunity to explore her own family’s legacy while also looking at the spirit of giving through history. So, tracing how her loved ones made the journey to America in the 1890s at the same time philanthropist Lena Sittig space was creating what is now considered to be the modern toy drive, really hit home how interconnected the mission is.

“I learned that my grandmother was coming over on a ship at 16 years old, right when Lena was having her idea for this,” she shared. “It’s kind of crazy how the world intertwines, and it just reminds you that you're just such a small part of such a bigger picture.”

It’s especially poignant as diving back into her roots has not always been a focal point for Gellar.

“It's funny, I didn't really spend that much time thinking about my history and my ancestry because I try so hard to live in the moment,” she explained. “And when Ancestry came to me and talked about what they wanted to do, I thought, ‘What a great idea to be able to learn acts of kindness, acts of goodness that your family may have been a part of that you never knew.’”

As the Cruel Intentions alum knows, ‘tis the season to pay it forward. “The holiday season gets so dramatic—presents and all that,” she noted. “And I always look for what are the things that you could give someone that are really meaningful.”

So, the 49-year-old posited, “What's more meaningful than learning about where you came from and your family and things you may not have known?”

To Gellar, it all comes back to Lena Sittig and her Brooklyn Christmas Tree Society, and how her idea is sparking change so many generations later. In fact, the Ringer actress teamed up with Ancestry to fulfill Christmas lists for Children’s Aid.

“So often, I think we think, ‘Well, I'm one person. What can I do?’ And then you see something like that, and you realize, oh wow, one person can do a lot,” she told E!. “But then to take it that step further, and maybe there's people in her family had no idea they were related to her.”

“Can you imagine going back in your history and finding out that one person in your family was responsible for millions of children's gifts all over the world because they had this idea?” Gellar added. “I think it's really special.”

And it’s an experience Gellar wants to send far and wide, teasing what many of her loved ones—not to mention anyone looking to explore the impact their family has made on others—may be getting under the tree this year.

“There's something for me about the how tangible it was,” she admitted. “I saw signatures, I saw writing. it makes it seem just much more real to you than just getting an email that says, ‘You know you came from here’ like, seeing their actual signatures at Ellis Island. It's also something too, growing up in New York City, you forget about it. But this is the gateway.”

And for Gellar it also ended up being a sweet gateway into a piece of history she and Prinze didn’t realize they shared. For a deeper history of the longtime couple’s life together, keep reading…

#3504. Fiona the Hippo's Necropsy Results Revealed After Her Death

Fiona the Hippo's necropsy results found that no effort to save the animal would have worked after the beloved hippopotamus swallowed a knit hat.

The Cincinnati Zoo shared Friday that her necropsy showed the hat had been lodged in the middle of her small intestine for days before she died.

To put that in perspective, the piece of clothing was located about 50 feet from the end of her intestines.

Cincinnati Zoo's director of animal health, Dr. Mike Wenninger, said ... "Upper and lower GI endoscopy were unable to reach the object. The location and anatomy made laparoscopic removal impossible. No treatment aside from supportive care had any chance for success, and the necropsy confirmed that no amount of supportive care would have worked."

We reported earlier ... Fiona ate the hat last week after a child threw it into the enclosure. In a freak accident, the hat managed to hit a fan and slip past a gap to find its way into Fiona's habitat.

Unfortunately, vets who tried to remove it were unsuccessful.

#3498. 'Ghost Accounts' Are Putting Your Security at Risk, but You Can Protect Yourself

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

In all the years you've been online, you've likely created more accounts than you can remember, whether to shop on a website you made one purchase from, sign up for a newsletter you've since stopped reading, or download apps for school or work that you no longer need.

These so-called "ghost accounts"—all the old, forgotten logins that are still active but not in use—could expose your data in the event of a breach, increasing the risk of your information being used in malicious ways. That's why it's important to go through the effort to find and delete dormant accounts. Here's how to get started.

As McAfee describes, ghost accounts may retain lots of sensitive data, such as your contact details (phone numbers, emails, and addresses), purchase histories, payment details, and passwords. While this doesn't mean your information is sure to be compromised, the more places it lives, the more opportunities there are for bad actors to get ahold of it.

You're less likely to be keeping tabs on activity in older accounts, which may also have weak or reused passwords that haven't been updated in years. If that company or service experiences a data breach, not only is your stored data there exposed, but that information (including your password) can be used to access other accounts using tactics like credential stuffing and phishing. This also increases the risk of identity theft, as threat actors can use your name, birth date, and other information to open fraudulent accounts.

Unfortunately, finding and removing forgotten accounts can be tedious. If you have a password manager, the easiest way to start is to audit older items as well as look at security reports that identify weak or reused passwords, as well as data breaches that have impacted your accounts. If you've saved credentials in your browser keychain, go through the same process to find dormant accounts.

The next place to look is in your email: Search for account confirmation and verification emails as well as password resets using keywords like "verify your email," "free trial," "welcome," "confirm your account," or "sign up." Add a date filter to narrow down older accounts. Do this across all of your email addresses.

Once you've found accounts you no longer use, the next step is to deactivate or delete them, which you may be able to do through the settings or by reaching out to customer support. At the very least, remove all identifying information and change the password, and if possible, update the address to a burner using your browser's or password manager's hide-my-email feature. If you no longer have access to an old account, that doesn't mean it's been deactivated and your information removed, so you may need to reach out to customer support to find out how to access and delete it.
